value.first: I'd use the Ferber method, also called graduated check-ins. She sleeps in her own crib in her own room from night 1, and you check on her at set intervals instead of staying with her. It's one of the best-studied sleep methods there is, and the five-year follow-up found no differences, positive or negative, for kids who did it. If she's in a toddler bed rather than a crib, the chair method fits better, since she can follow you out.
value.second: Nights 1-3: do the same short routine (bath, book, bed), put her in her crib awake, say your goodnight phrase, and leave. If she cries, wait 3, then 5, then 10 minutes on night 1. Use 5/10/12 on night 2 and 10/12/15 on night 3. Checks are 1-2 minutes with a calm phrase and no pickup. Use the same sequence for night wakings, and never bring her back to your bed. Expect night 2 or 3 to be worse - that's the old habit breaking.
value.third: Nights 4-7: keep stretching the waits, from 12/15/17 on night 4 up to 20/25/30 by night 7. You'll know it's working when she falls asleep faster and wakes less. Many kids settle within the week. If she snores, gasps, or pauses breathing in her sleep, that's worth a doctor's look. I'll check in Thursday.
